brief: Academy Securities (Peter Tchir) sees synchronized stress in Treasuries, European sovereigns, and credit. On Treasuries: yields jumped (10s from 4.6% on August 25 to 5.27% by Friday, including an intraday swing from 5.15% to 5.27% after the jobs report) despite thin real bearish positioning - longs are low-conviction, TLT shares outstanding sit near multi-year highs, and sentiment skews bullish-to-neutral. The author attributes the move to thin true liquidity and systematic momentum algos where selling begets selling, layered on a root cause of a global sovereign-and-corporate debt supply glut (record HY and $10bn corporate deals), not inflation or Fed independence. In Europe, French and Italian yields have diverged from German yields; the author links this to France's deficit tracking near 5% versus the EU's 3% target and suspects an unwind of trades that treated French/Italian risk as equivalent to German risk. In credit, CDX widened from 50 to 60bps in two weeks versus OAS moving only 75 to 82bps, and PSKY's bonds fell to 95% of par before recovering to 96.5% (about $140mm of mark-to-market loss), though HY/IG ETFs still trade at NAV. The author ends neutral on rates but nervous, flagging CDX's decoupling from a rising S&P 500.

cards.anchor: The root causes have far less to do with economic variables, inflation, and Fed independence, and much more to do with a global supply glut.
